Block bootstrap of site frequency spectra

Source: R/bootstrap_sfs.R
bootstrap_sfs.Rd

Compute bootstrap replicates of the site frequency spectra of pop_sfs(), pairwise_pop_sfs() and nwise_pop_sfs(), by resampling blocks of loci with replacement. Replicates are used to estimate the uncertainty of statistics computed from the spectra, or of the parameters of demographic models fitted with dadi, moments or fastsimcoal2 (see write_sfs() to write the replicates in their formats).

Usage

bootstrap_pop_sfs(.x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gen_tbl'
bootstrap_pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_bootstrap = 100,
  block_size,
  size_unit = c("snp", "cM", "bp"),
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  ...
)

bootstrap_pairwise_pop_sfs(.x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gen_tbl'
bootstrap_pairwise_pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_bootstrap = 100,
  block_size,
  size_unit = c("snp", "cM", "bp"),
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  fastest = c("last", "first"),
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  ...
)

bootstrap_nwise_pop_sfs(.x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gen_tbl'
bootstrap_nwise_pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_bootstrap = 100,
  block_size,
  size_unit = c("snp", "cM", "bp"),
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  fastest = c("last", "first"),
  max_cells = 1e+07,
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  ...
)

Arguments

.x

a gen_tibble, grouped by population (or, for bootstrap_pop_sfs(), ungrouped to compute the spectrum of all individuals).

...

other arguments passed to specific methods, currently unused.

n_bootstrap

the number of bootstrap replicates.

block_size

the size of the blocks of loci that are resampled.

size_unit

the unit of block_size: "snp" (the default), "cM" or "bp".

n_proj

the number of allele copies to project each population to: either a single value used for all populations, a vector with one value per population (in the order of the groups), or a vector named with the group labels. If NULL (the default), each population is projected to the number of allele copies that maximises its number of segregating sites (see pop_sfs_preview()).

folded

boolean, whether to fold the spectrum (the default, as the ancestral allele is not usually known). If FALSE, the spectrum is polarised with ancestral.

ancestral

the ancestral allele of each locus, used to polarise unfolded spectra: either the name of a column of the loci table (see show_loci()), or a character vector with one allele per locus (in the order of the loci table). Loci whose ancestral allele is missing (NA) or is neither of their alleles are dropped. If NULL (the default), the reference allele is taken to be ancestral, as in easySFS. Ignored, with a warning, for folded spectra.

type

the type of object to return, either "tidy" (the default) or "array".

n_cores

number of cores to be used, it defaults to bigstatsr::nb_cores()

fastest

the order of the cells of each spectrum in the tidy output: "last" (the default) keeps the order of the populations, so that the rows are sorted by the number of allele copies in the first population, then in the second (the number of copies in the second population changes fastest, as in the files written by dadi and easySFS); "first" makes the number of copies in the first population change fastest.

max_cells

the maximum number of cells of all the replicates (the number of cells of the joint spectrum times n_bootstrap); an error is raised for more cells, to avoid running out of memory.

Value

If type = "tidy", a tibble with the columns of the tidy output of pop_sfs(), pairwise_pop_sfs() or nwise_pop_sfs(), and a column replicate (after the group columns) with the number of the replicate. If type = "array", a list with one element per replicate, each of which is what pop_sfs(), pairwise_pop_sfs() or nwise_pop_sfs() return with type = "array" (lists of sfs objects, or an sfs object). In both cases, the attribute bootstrap_blocks is a matrix with the number of times each block (columns, numbered in the order in which they appear in the loci table) was drawn in each replicate (rows), and the tibble also has the attributes n_proj and folded.

Details

The loci are divided into non-overlapping blocks that never span more than one chromosome, defined as in the jackknife_* functions (e.g. jackknife_pop_tajimas_d()): blocks of block_size SNPs, base pairs or centiMorgans (the latter requires the genetic_dist column of the loci table). Blocks should be larger than the extent of linkage disequilibrium, so that they are approximately independent. Each replicate draws, with replacement, as many blocks as there are (as the bootstrap of dadi, Misc.bootstraps_from_dd_chunks()). With block_size = 1 and size_unit = "snp", single SNPs are resampled (as the --resample-vcf option of easySFS), which ignores linkage.

A spectrum is a sum over loci, so the spectrum of a replicate is the sum of the spectra of the blocks it drew (counting each block as many times as it was drawn). The genotypes are therefore read only once, to compute the spectrum of each block. Missing data are dealt with by projection, as in pop_sfs(), with the same projections (n_proj) for all replicates: if n_proj is NULL, they are chosen from all the loci with pop_sfs_preview(). The blocks are drawn with the random number generator of R, so use set.seed() to make the replicates reproducible.

See also

pop_sfs(), write_sfs(), jackknife_stats_generic()

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

set.seed(1)
# resample blocks of 2 SNPs
boot <- example_gt %>%
  bootstrap_pop_sfs(n_bootstrap = 10, block_size = 2, n_proj = 2)
boot
#> # A tibble: 90 × 5
#>    group replicate allele_count n_sites masked
#>    <chr>     <int>        <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#>  1 pop1          1            0    3.47 TRUE  
#>  2 pop1          1            1    2.53 FALSE 
#>  3 pop1          1            2    0    TRUE  
#>  4 pop1          2            0    3.6  TRUE  
#>  5 pop1          2            1    2.4  FALSE 
#>  6 pop1          2            2    0    TRUE  
#>  7 pop1          3            0    4    TRUE  
#>  8 pop1          3            1    2    FALSE 
#>  9 pop1          3            2    0    TRUE  
#> 10 pop1          4            0    3.2  TRUE  
#> # ℹ 80 more rows

# the 95% interval of the number of sites in each cell
boot %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group, allele_count) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    lower = stats::quantile(n_sites, 0.025),
    upper = stats::quantile(n_sites, 0.975)
  )
#> `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
#> ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by group and allele_count.
#> ℹ Output is grouped by group.
#> ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
#> ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(group, allele_count))` for per-operation grouping
#>   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#> # Groups:   group [3]
#>   group allele_count lower upper
#>   <chr>        <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 pop1             0  2.96  3.91
#> 2 pop1             1  2.09  3.04
#> 3 pop1             2  0     0   
#> 4 pop2             0  3.5   4.5 
#> 5 pop2             1  1.5   2.5 
#> 6 pop2             2  0     0   
#> 7 pop3             0  1.5   4.5 
#> 8 pop3             1  1.5   4.5 
#> 9 pop3             2  0     0   

# the joint spectra of each pair, as arrays
boot_2d <- example_gt %>%
  bootstrap_pairwise_pop_sfs(
    n_bootstrap = 5, block_size = 2, n_proj = 2,
    type = "array"
  )
boot_2d[[1]]$pop1.pop2
#> # A folded site frequency spectrum of 2 populations
#> # Allele copies: pop1 = 2, pop2 = 2
#> # Loci used: 6 (dropped for missing data: 0)
#>     pop2
#> pop1         0 1         2
#>    0 0.9666667 1 0.4833333
#>    1 2.0666667 1 0.0000000
#>    2 0.4833333 0 0.0000000
